newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close higher, Korean Air slumps.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close higher, Korean Air slumps.

text.p: Seoul stocks ended stronger for the third consecutive day on Wednesday as punters built up more confidence over the future market direction with fears of more corporate failures easing, brokers said.
But shares in Korean Air Lines and its affiliates fell as a KAL jumbo jet crashed on the Pacifici Island of Guam.
Some Kia Group shares also dived without fresh developments to help finance the troubled group.
The composite stock index closed up 4.79 points to 745.65 with 34.05 million shares changing hands. Gains were seen evenly spread out as risers outpaced losers, 423 to 348.
"Investors believe they can afford to worry less over corporate failures now that Kia was protected from bankruptcy for two months," said a Hanyang Securities broker.
Lim Chong-woo of Ssangyong Investment Securities said: "The index has been rising with investors feeling more comfortable after firming support at 720 points."
Brokers said the rise could also be viewed as "technical," but the market needed a booster to maintain the gain on Thursday.
Core blue chips such as Samsung Electronics and SK Telecom continued to rise. Samsung gained 300 won to 69,300 and SK Telecom rose 5,000 to 463,000.
Brokers said selected low-price stocks, which had fallen sharply in recent days, rebounded on bargain hunting. Shinho Petrochemical Co Ltd added 290 won to close at its upper limit of 3,940.
However, Korean Air and its affiliates slumped on concerns about worsening global image of the airliner and possible higher insurance costs following the plane crash, brokers said.

Korean Air, an affiliate of Hanjin Group, lost 800 won to 15,300. Orient Fire Insurance, a Hanjin Group affiliate and also the airliner's insurer, fell 400 to 21,500 and Korean Air Terminal was down 700 won to 27,900.
A Korean Air jumbo jet carrying 254 people crashed on Guam early on Wednesday. More than 200 people were feared dead.

Brokers said shares of most Kia Group units dropped sharply. But Kia Precision surged 670 won to close at its upper limit of 9,070 on a rumour that the nation's two carmakers Hyundai Motor and Daewoo Motor planned to buy stakes of the firm.
But a Kia Group spokesman denied the market speculation.
"That is not true. There was no talk of such move," he said.
Kia Motors lost 1,100 won to its limit low of 12,900, Asia Motors fell 400 to its lower limit of 4,620 and Kia Motor Sales was down 400 to its limit low of 4,660.
Last week the Kia Group said Hyundai Motor and Daewoo Motor had agreed in principle to buy stakes in Kia Steel.
